bib.title: FP8-LM: Training FP8 Large Language Models

question: Can FP8 be used not only for GEMM compute but also for gradients, optimizer states and distributed training of LLMs, cutting memory and communication without losing accuracy or changing hyper-parameters?
hypothesis: Most variables in LLM training (gradients, optimizer moments) can use low-precision FP8 without hurting accuracy and without hyper-parameter changes.
contributions: A new FP8 mixed-precision training framework that unlocks 8-bit weights, gradients, optimizer and distributed training gradually in an add-on fashion, as a drop-in replacement for 16/32-bit mixed precision with no hyper-parameter changes, with a PyTorch implementation.

A family of GPT-style models (7B to 175B) trained with FP8 for pre-training and fine-tuning (SFT, RLHF), with FP8 tensor, pipeline and sequence parallelism, and an open-source FP8 GPT codebase built on Megatron-LM.

method.summary: A three-level FP8 automatic mixed-precision framework (MS-AMP): FP8 gradients with all-reduce using automatic scaling and a shared minimum scaling factor, an FP8 Adam optimizer (FP8 first moment, FP16 second moment, FP16 master weights with tensor scaling), and FP8 tensor/sequence parallelism plus a greedy whole-tensor ZeRO distribution. Compared against BF16 Megatron-LM and Nvidia Transformer Engine on GPT models of 125M to 175B parameters, in pre-training, SFT and RLHF.
method.task: next-token pretraining, instruction tuning (SFT) and RLHF (PPO) under FP8 mixed precision

training.objective: autoregressive next-token prediction (pre-training); SFT as Vicuna-v1.1; PPO for RLHF following AlpacaFarm
training.optimizer: FP8 Adam with decoupled weight decay (AdamW), beta1=0.9, beta2=0.95
training.lr_schedule: cosine-like, final lr is 10% of maximal
training.precision: FP8 compute (GEMM), FP8 gradients and all-reduce, FP8 first moment, FP16 second moment, FP16 master weights with tensor scaling; baselines BF16-FP32 and FP32
training.hardware: Azure NDv5 H100 GPU platform (80GB H100); GPU counts: 32 for 7B and 4096-context test, 16 DP x TP2 for 13B, TP8xPP4xDP4 for 175B (128 GPUs inferred from parallelism product)

other.auto_scaling: mu halves next step if fraction of values at FP8 max exceeds 0.001%, otherwise increases exponentially to 2 over 1,000 steps
other.gradient_all_reduce: global minimum scaling factor s'_g = min(s'_1..s'_N) shared across GPUs, then standard NCCL all-reduce, s = N * s'_g
other.bytes_per_param: 16 bytes for FP32 Adam mixed precision (Eq 7), 6 bytes for FP8 optimizer (Eq 8): 2 master + 1 gradient + 1 + 2 Adam states
other.optimization_levels: three levels adding FP8 communication, optimizer and distributed parallel training incrementally
other.zero: greedy whole-tensor assignment, largest tensors first to the GPU with least memory (Alg 1)
other.figure_1_data: max model size on H100 80GB clusters, read from Fig 1 not extractable as numbers

limits: Largest model (175B) is trained for only 40B tokens, 'sufficient for evaluating system performance'; accuracy at full scale and long training is not shown.
Downstream accuracy shown only for 7B and 13B (Table 2); no zero-shot results for 175B; SFT and RLHF only at 7B scale (LLaMA-7B).
No seeds, no variance, no significance tests; differences like 58.0 vs 58.4 are single runs.
Requires Hopper (H100) hardware for FP8; weights and data mix not released.
Authors state future work: scale up model size and steps, multimodal models, low-bit deployment on edge devices.
This is a training-time method: it says nothing about FP8 inference or post-training quantization of deployed models.
Speed comparison to BF16 at 175B uses a larger micro batch (4) for FP8 than BF16 (1); at equal micro BS 1 the gain is +21%.

terms.definition: decoupling the influence of data precision on parameters such as weights, gradients, optimizer states, and assigning reduced precision to components that are not precision sensitive
